name: Chakravageswarar Temple, Tiruchakkarappalli
deity: Shiva as Chakravageswarar, with the goddess Devanayaki
period: Early Chola temple of the Kaveri delta, sung in the Tevaram, developed from the Aditya Chola era (9th century)
summary: At Chakkarapalli near Ayyampettai, Shiva is Chakravageswarar, worshipped in tradition by Vishnu who received his discus here; the temple is a Tevaram shrine and one of the Chakkarapalli Sapta Sthanam.

sections.history: Tiruchakkarappalli, now better known by the nearby town of Ayyampettai, is a Shaiva village of the Kaveri delta and a Paadal Petra Sthalam praised by Appar and Thirugnana Sambandar. The Lord is worshipped as Chakravageswarar, with the goddess Devanayaki, and the sanctum enshrines a swayambhu linga. The temple's development traces to the age of Aditya Chola I, with substantial expansion under Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, whose reigns raised many of the delta's shrines to their mature form. The village name, Chakkarapalli, is explained by the tradition that Vishnu obtained his discus here.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the Dravidian manner, with a gopuram, pillared halls and a prakara around the sanctum of Chakravageswarar. The goddess Devanayaki has her own shrine, and the usual parivara deities of a Shiva temple stand around the courtyard. The old stonework of the early Chola core is wrapped in the additions of later reigns, giving the temple the layered character typical of the long-endowed shrines of the delta.
sections.legends: Two stories are told of the temple's name. In one, Vishnu worshipped Shiva here and received from him the Sudarshana, the discus with which he guards the worlds, so that the Lord became Chakravageswarar and the village Chakkarapalli, the town of the discus. In another, the chakravaka bird is said to have worshipped Shiva at this place. The temple is also one of the Chakkarapalli Sapta Sthanam, a group of seven shrines linked to the worship of the Saptamatrikas.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri, the monthly Pradosham, and the Tamil month festivals are observed, along with the car festival and the Sapta Sthanam observances shared among the seven local shrines. Festival dates follow the Tamil calendar, so confirm them locally.
sections.experience: Chakravageswarar is an unhurried delta temple, easily reached from the Thanjavur–Kumbakonam road and often visited with the other Tevaram shrines of the region. Devotees worship the swayambhu linga and the goddess Devanayaki, and recall the tradition of Vishnu receiving his discus here, which gives the modest village temple its distinctive name and story.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Chakkarapalli is near Ayyampettai in Papanasam taluk, Thanjavur district, between Thanjavur and Kumbakonam. Ayyampettai has a railway station on the Thanjavur–Kumbakonam line; Tiruchirappalli airport is about 60 km away. Local buses and autos serve the village.
